The story takes the familiar "switched at birth" trope and completely subverts it in a thought-provoking way, offering a unique perspective on parenthood, genetics, and identity. Instead of reacting with horror and demanding her biological child back, the protagonist—an art provenance expert whose entire career is built on verifying authentic lineages—consciously chooses to keep the "forged" baby. This presents the reader with the original and challenging idea that escaping one's own anxious "genetic lineage" and embracing an undocumented, unknown future can be a source of profound relief and liberation rather than tragedy.
